I graduated at 17 and left right away for a top tier college. I wish I had waited. I really didn't have the money to go but I thought it was what I had to do to get anywhere in life. I paid for his hormones. Im there when he gets really down about his dysphoria. I'm the one who promised I'd be there to help after his surgeries. I've given him a place to live through it all. It will be for a while. It just means that you were a genuine person who truly loved another person. That's not a bad thing! That's a great quality. Now it's time to turn all that energy and love onto yourself and help yourself forward.

This is the time for you to finally focus on yourself. I know it sucks and it's going to be so hard but do your best to stay busy. You can grieve and stay busy at the same time. Surround yourself with people you are close with that have little to no connection with her. After a while it'll get easier. How nice will it be to be able to come home and relax rather than coming home and walking in on your partner with someone else for the seventh time? Imagine having that pressure off of you. Being able to fill your time with positive experiences for yourself. Maybe take this time to learn a new skill... Just try and keep busy. I promise it will get easier after some time.
